items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall that to solve a linear equation, we isolate the variable by reversing the operations applied to it.

Content:
So if a variable is multiplied by a number, we use the opposite operation, which is division.

Content:
Whatever operation we perform on one side of the equation, we must perform the same operation on the other side to keep the equation balanced.

Content:
For example, consider the equation

Content:
[MATH: 6x = 42.]

Content:
Since [MATH: x] is multiplied by [MATH: 6,] we divide both sides by [MATH: 6]:

Content:
[MATH: 6x|= 42; 6x ÷ 6|= 42 ÷ 6]

Content:
Now simplify each side:

Content:
[MATH: (6 ÷ 6)x|= 42 ÷ 6; 1x|= 7; x|= 7.]

Content:
Note: If the variable appears on the right-hand side (e.g., [MATH: 15=3y]), you may first swap the left and right sides of the equation to get [MATH: 3y=15.]

To solve a linear equation, we isolate the variable by reversing the operations applied to it, performing each inverse operation on both sides of the equation step by step.

In this case, the variable [MATH: m] is multiplied by [MATH: 4.] To isolate [MATH: m,] we perform the opposite operation, which is dividing by [MATH: 4.] So, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: 4{:}]

[MATH: 4m|= 28; 4m ÷ 4|= 28 ÷ 4; (4 ÷ 4)m|= 7; 1m|= 7; m|= 7]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:

Content:
Whatever operation we perform on one side of the equation, we must perform the same operation on the other side to keep the equation balanced.

Content:
For example, consider the equation

Content:
[MATH: 6x = 42.]

Content:

Content:

Content:
Now simplify each side:

Content:
[MATH: (6 ÷ 6)x|= 42 ÷ 6; 1x|= 7; x|= 7.]
